author: "Yun Jiang"
include-in-header:
  text: |
    <link rel="icon" href="data:image/svg+xml,<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 100 100'><text y='.9em' font-size='90'>🧬</text></svg>">

## objective

Split each position's `mismatch` count in the `--error-out` Parquet
(`{p}.error.parquet`) by the read (destination) base, adding four columns:
`to_a`, `to_c`, `to_g`, `to_t`. No `to_n` (user decision).

## scope

- In-scope: `ErrorStatsCollector` positional tally, `PositionalErrorStats`
  writer, unit tests, `docs/usage.qmd` table + semantics note.
- Out-of-scope: the other six error-stat outputs, `mismatch_matrix`,
  `qc-summary` (unchanged — per-base totals keep their meaning), CLI surface
  (no new flags; the columns are always present).

## semantics

- `to_x` = in-region substitutions at that 1-based position whose read base is
  x, regardless of the reference base (a ref-N ref with read-A lands in
  `to_a`).
- A substitution whose read base is N counts in `mismatch` but in no `to_*`
  column, so `to_a+to_c+to_g+to_t` can be below `mismatch`.

## steps

1. Add `to_a/to_c/to_g/to_t` int fields to `_PositionalErrorCounts`
   (`src/sam_tagger/stats/error_stats.py`).
2. In the `*` branch of `tally_from_parsed`, increment the field matching
   `read_idx` 0–3 (skip 4 = N) after `entry.mismatches += 1`.
3. Extend `PositionalErrorStats` (`src/sam_tagger/parquet_writer.py`) to a
   9-column schema, all four new columns `UInt64`.
4. Pass the four counts in `_write_error_stats` (dense loop unchanged).
5. Update/extend tests in `tests/test_stats.py` (mismatch tally asserts the
   `to_*` split, new N-base test, `write_all_seven` asserts the parquet
   schema and values) and in `tests/test_parquet_writer.py` (the
   `PositionalErrorStats.add` signature and the 9-column width).
6. Update `docs/usage.qmd`: contents cell + N-semantics note.

## files

- `src/sam_tagger/stats/error_stats.py`
- `src/sam_tagger/parquet_writer.py`
- `tests/test_stats.py`
- `tests/test_parquet_writer.py`
- `docs/usage.qmd`

## risks

- Schema widening is visible to strict-schema downstream consumers
  (additive only; name-based readers unaffected).
- Larger row width in `error.parquet`; new columns are mostly zeros, and
  Parquet run-length encoding keeps growth small.

## verification

- `pixi run -e dev test` green (all existing + new tests).
- `pixi run -e dev lint` green.
- New test asserts: `*ac` → `to_c=1`; read-N → no `to_*`; ref-N/read-A →
  `to_a=1`; written parquet carries the 9-column schema.
